bucket_backend.description: Specifies the database backend to use for storage, with an option for default (represented by an empty string), 'mongodb', or 'influxdb'.
bucket_backend.title: Bucket Backend

bucket_config.description: Configuration schema for a data bucket specifying how data is sourced and updated. This schema supports multiple source types including devices and MQTT topics, each with its own set of required properties.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data sourced from a device. This requires specifying the device, user, resource, update interval, and optional tags.

device.description: The unique identifier for the device.

interval.description: The time between updates, in seconds.

resource.description: The specific resource from the device being tracked.

source.description: Indicates the data source is a device.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

update.description: Specifies that the bucket is updated at regular intervals.

user.description: The unique identifier for the user associated with this bucket.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data sourced from a device with event-based or no updates. This variation does not require an interval.

device.description: The unique identifier for the device.

resource.description: The specific resource from the device being tracked.

source.description: Indicates the data source is a device.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

update.description: Specifies how the bucket is updated: either by specific events or not updated automatically.

user.description: The unique identifier for the user associated with this bucket.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data sourced from an MQTT topic. This requires specifying the topic and allows optional tags.

source.description: Indicates the data source is an MQTT topic.

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

topic.description: The MQTT topic from which data is sourced.

oneOf.description: Configuration for data manually written or provided via an API. This variation only requires source specification and allows optional tags.

source.description: Indicates the data source is either manually written ('write') or sourced via an API ('api').

tags.description: A collection of tags for categorization, limited to 5.

bucket_config.title: Bucket Config

bucket_retention.description: Configuration schema for data bucket retention policy.

period.description: The duration of the retention period. 0 for unlimited retention.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the retention period.

bucket_retention.title: Bucket Retention

product_conditional_icon.title: Product Conditional Icon

type.description: Product type that determines the device status view

projects_ids.description: A collection of unique project IDs, ensuring no duplicates within the array.

items.description: An array of unique project identifiers, each following a 'username@project' format with each part limited to 32 alphanumeric characters, underscores or hyphens.

resource_description.description: A brief description of the resource, providing context or additional information, limited to 255 characters.

resource_id.description: A unique identifier for resources, consisting of alphanumeric characters, underscores, or hyphens, and limited to 32 characters.
resource_id.title: Resource ID

resource_name.description: The name of the resource, limited to 255 characters. It can include any character.
resource_name.title: Resource Name

brand.description: The domain the brand applies to (e.g. iot.example.com): the console is branded for requests to that host. Point the domain to this server and register it in domains to get its certificate.

domain.description: Hostname to serve with its own TLS certificate, e.g. iot.example.com. Before verifying, point it to this server (A/AAAA record to its IP, or CNAME to its hostname) and make sure port 80 is reachable from the internet: POST /v1/domains/{domain}/verify gets a Let's Encrypt certificate through an HTTP-01 challenge (a *.wildcard needs the DNS-01 challenge, only on Thinger-hosted servers). Certificates renew automatically while the DNS keeps pointing here. Brand the console on it by creating a brand with the same id.

host.description: Hostname of the server. Hosts register themselves when they start.

get.description: Server output (stdout and stderr) of the host. A websocket upgrade streams new lines live; a plain GET returns the last lines as text/plain. Reads the logs of the Docker container the server runs in (deployment.container_name, default "thinger"); other cluster hosts are proxied.

parameters.description: Plain GET: number of last lines (1-5000, default 200).
parameters.name: lines

parameters.description: Plain GET: prefix each line with its timestamp.
parameters.name: timestamps

parameters.description: Plain GET: only lines after this unix timestamp, or this many seconds ago when below 31536000.

schema.description: Merged (RFC 7386 merge patch: null removes a key) into the host custom settings, on top of the provider settings. Changes apply after POST /v1/hosts/{host}/restart. Ports are strings: numbers are ignored by the server.

accounts.description: Accounts and limits. Brands can override the sign-up and login keys per domain.

admin_emails.description: Email addresses whose accounts become admins.

identity_providers.description: Identity provider ids offered on login; empty offers every enabled one.

limits.description: Per collection: {"<collection>": {"max_count": n}} with -1 = unlimited and 0 = disabled. Collections: access_tokens, buckets, dashboards, devices, endpoints, plugins, projects, projects_members, storages, alarms_rules, alarms_instances, syncs, types, groups, products, proxies, oauth_clients, identity_providers (default 0: set it to enable them). Also buckets.retention {period, unit} and buckets / endpoints min_interval. Accounts can override them with their own limits.

required_email_domains.description: Only these email domains can sign up.

export.description: Where bucket exports are written: type filesystem ({filesystem: {export_path}}) or s3 ({s3: {bucket_id, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key, aws_region}}).

storage.description: Where bucket data is stored: default is mongodb, influxdb or dynamodb, each with its own connection settings (mongodb {connection_string, max_retention, default_retention}, influxdb {host, port, username, password}, dynamodb {table_name, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key, aws_region}).

contact_email.description: The account registered with this email becomes admin; also {{admin}} in email templates.

email.description: Server mail settings, used when a brand has no custom email.

dynamic_port_range_start.description: First port given to proxies without a fixed port (default 50000).

client_ca_certs.description: PEM certificates to accept as client certificates.

Register https://<brand domain>/oauth/callback as redirect URI in the provider, check it with POST /v1/identity_providers/{id}/test, and offer it on a domain with the brand config accounts.federated_login / accounts.identity_providers.
